name: Aurora Fjord
description: Night fjord under domain-warped aurora curtains: layered FBM mountain silhouettes, twinkling Voronoi stars, a rippled lake mirroring the sky, rendered into a high-res Feedback target with multi-level bloom, chromatic aberration, grain and vignette. Tweak it in the Parameters panel (P): Aurora, Scene, Post and Music.

data.text:
# Aurora Fjord
A night fjord under domain-warped aurora curtains: layered FBM mountain silhouettes, twinkling Voronoi stars, low mist, and everything mirrored in rippling water. A purely 2D shader, no raymarching.
Reacts to music: open the audio menu → Mic (curtains glow on the mids and ripple on the highs, bright stars twinkle on the beat).
## Tweak it in the Parameters panel
Press P (or the sliders button in the top bar): Aurora, Scene, Post and Music settings with pretty names; hover a name for what it does, double-click a slider to reset it.
Double-click a group box to open it, Esc to come back.

## Water Reflection
Below the horizon the UV is mirrored and wobbled by FBM ripples (WaveUV), so the whole sky and mountains reflect in the fjord; the water then gets a dark tint.

## Aurora
Two curtains: a domain-warped FBM defines each curtain's wavy bottom edge; above it, exponential falloff × vertical FBM rays × a color ramp (green → violet) give the glowing drapes.

## Mountains
Three FBM ridgelines (far, mid, near) cut out silhouettes with smoothsteps, each shaded with haze, snow and rim light, layered front to back over the sky.

## Render Targets
The tonemapped frame and a three-buffer bright-pass blur chain (Feedback nodes) for the bloom.

## Music
Audio level gates everything: with the audio off or silent, drive = 0 and the fjord looks exactly as before. drive = music × smoothstep(level).
- Mids: the aurora curtains glow up to +30%.
- Highs: the domain warp deepens (strength 0.5 → 0.56), so the drapes ripple with hats and cymbals.
- Beat: the bright stars twinkle (×2.4, short attack and decay).
Beat-phase couplings (star twinkle) are also multiplied by the beat tracker's confidence (Beat.confidence = u_beatConfidence: 0 with the audio off, ~1 once the beat locks, 1 with the metronome) and run on the stable beat clock with its certainty gate (Beat.gate / BeatEnvelope gate: fade, u_beatTrust): after a track change the clock holds the old tempo, then glides to the new one without jumps, and these couplings fade out until the new beat is trusted. Level and band couplings (mid glow, high ripple) are not.
